newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hold firm in late trade, eye Wall St.
newsitem.headline: German shares hold firm in late trade, eye Wall St.

text.p: The German share market held firm at higher levels in late afternoon dealings on Monday, although dealers were keeping a cautious eye on Wall Street, which could risk a correction after Friday's bull run.

"Of course we'll take our cue from Wall Street, although it's not really justified. We have more than enough reasons at home to give us an upward trand and I believe these will win out," said one Frankfurt dealer.
The IBIS DAX index was up 22.51 points at 2,885.77 at 1350 GMT, some four points ahead of its mid-afternoon bourse close.
March DAX futures were up 20.5 at 2,902.5 points.
German shares were lifted from the start by the Dow Jones' index's 1.6 percent gain on Friday and the firmer dollar.
But positive news on the German automotive sector from the Detroit Auto Show gave car stocks a particular boost.

Daimler-Benz was up 2.80 marks at 108.60 after its Mercedes luxury car unit, which accounts for most of the parent company's profits, told reporters it expected U.S. sales in 1997 at over 100,000 units.
Volkswagen AG rose 10 marks to 651.25, boosted by a report that it was planning to build a new mini car to compete in the small-car market.
BMW lagged behind, slipping 5.30 marks to 1,050.70 marks in late dealings.
"BMW just isn't viewed as having as many good model ideas as the others at the moment."

Among non-blue chips, tyre maker Continental AG also performed well, rising 85 pfennigs to 29.85, which dealers attributed to the upsurge in demand for winter tyres during the current prolonged snowbound period in Germany.
Diversified utility Veba AG was up 1.62 marks at 91.10 after announcing an acquisition in cable television.
The company said its Vebacom GmbH unit, a German-British alliance, would buy Urbana Systemtechnik AG.
Many dealers said the market's overall mood was bullish, given hopes for a broad economic recovery in Germany this year and better profits from top industrial companies.
"I think 3,000 (points) is a totally realistic goal for the DAX and it's not too far off," said one dealer.
Keen attention will be paid to German jobless and GDP data for 1996 which are due for release on Thursday.
